# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 7

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey — I can only feel the bomb, and right now my hands report nothing: no wires, no display, no light, nothing under my fingers yet. I have no information to act on and no received messages to respond to.

I should not cut anything. I'll wait and listen for what the others have found, since Deaf can see the bomb and Mute reads the manual, and their words will reach me next round.

```

```

TURN 2

DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Bomb reads: display shows 1, light is orange. Seven wires left to right: 1 white, 2 blue, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 yellow, 7 green. Mute, read the manual and gesture the rule to me — I will relay it to Blind. Blind, hold on, rule incoming.
Deaf says to Blind: For your hands: wires in order are white, blue, orange, red, purple, yellow, green. Display is 1. Light is orange.

I now know the bomb's visible layout from Deaf: display shows 1, light is orange, and wires 1–7 are white, blue, orange, red, purple, yellow, green. But I still don't know the rule — Mute has the manual and Deaf said they'd relay it to me. I have nothing to cut yet. I should acknowledge I received the layout and wait for the rule, so Deaf knows the relay worked and doesn't waste a turn repeating.

I'll speak to Mute (my only voice channel) confirming receipt, and gesture to Deaf (and Mute) that I got it and am waiting for the rule.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I received the layout from Deaf: display 1, light orange, wires white blue orange red purple yellow green. I still need the rule from your manual. Please send it so it reaches me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?] 6:[?] 7:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute, I got seven fists — no meaning yet, we have no shared code. Let's set one. To give me a wire number, gesture that many ? (one finger). To say CUT gesture ? after the number; to say DO NOT CUT gesture ?. Example: wire 3 cut = ????. Please confirm you understand by gesturing ? alone. Then send the rule.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, hold. I am decoding the manual from Mute. Do not touch anything yet.

Deaf is trying to establish a code with Mute, but Deaf's message to me is just "hold." I have nothing new. I should confirm to Deaf that I'm holding, and I can help by proposing a clean shared code since I'm a channel between them — but I can only gesture to Deaf and speak to Mute.

Actually, the key issue: Deaf can see gestures but not hear; Mute can read the manual but can't speak and can't be heard by Deaf except via... wait. Mute can gesture. Deaf can see gestures. So Mute→Deaf works via gesture. Mute→me works via... Mute can't speak, and I can't see gestures. So Mute cannot reach me directly at all! The only way Mute's manual knowledge reaches me is through Deaf's speech (Deaf hears nothing though — Deaf is deaf). 

Wait, let me re-trace. Deaf can see but not hear. Mute can read manual but not speak or touch. Blind (me) can touch but not see.

Speech: whoever can hear receives words. Deaf cannot hear. So Deaf never receives speech. Mute can hear (Mute cannot speak but can hear). Blind can hear.

Gestures: whoever can see receives. Deaf can see. Mute can see. Blind cannot see.

So channels:
- Me (Blind) speak → Mute hears it. (Deaf can't hear.)
- Me (Blind) gesture → Deaf sees, Mute sees.
- Deaf speak → Mute hears, Blind hears. (Deaf speaks, others hear.)
- Deaf gesture → Mute sees, Blind can't.
- Mute gesture → Deaf sees, Blind can't.
- Mute speak → impossible.

So the manual rule from Mute must travel: Mute gesture → Deaf sees → Deaf speaks → I hear. That's the relay. Good, that's what Deaf is doing.

Now Deaf set up a code with Mute. That's fine. I just need to wait. But I can also help by confirming. Let me just acknowledge to Deaf that I'm holding and waiting, and encourage Mute to send the rule.

Actually I should be careful not to clutter. But a short confirmation is useful. I'll gesture to Deaf that I'm holding (👍), and speak to Mute that I'm waiting for the rule relayed through Deaf.

Let me keep it minimal.I've confirmed the channel structure: Mute's manual knowledge can only reach me via Mute→gesture→Deaf→speech→me. Deaf is setting up a gesture code with Mute and told me to hold. I have nothing to cut. I'll acknowledge the hold to Deaf and gently remind Mute that the rule needs to go through Deaf to reach me.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind holding. When you have the rule, gesture it to Deaf so Deaf can speak it to me. I cannot see your gestures directly.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Rule decoded: CUT wire 7 — the seventh from the left, the last one. Its colour is green. Count to the seventh wire and cut it.

I now have everything: display 1, light orange, wires white-blue-orange-red-purple-yellow-green, and the rule says cut wire 7 (green). I'm the only one who can act. I should cut wire 7.

But wait — I should double-check the rule makes sense. The rule was decoded via a gesture code between Mute and Deaf that they just invented this round. There's risk of miscommunication. However, Deaf explicitly restated it in plain words with redundancy: "wire 7 — the seventh from the left, the last one. Its colour is green." That's consistent and matches the layout. I'll trust it and cut position 7.

I'll also confirm to the others what I did.

```
act(op="cut", position=7)
speak(to="mute", text="Cutting wire 7, the green one, as the rule says.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤟", "✊"])
```
